recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless the work group makes a new current-version decision to replace the contextual Resource language link with a direct All Languages ValueSet link.
issue_request: FHIR-18484 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core narrative correction asking to fix two links in the narrative language sentence: the resource language element should link to Resource.language, and the language-of-resource link was resolved to point at the language ValueSet used at the time.
initial_application: The Jira comment records GH#baf7726692. Commit baf77266921802b87b627274b31a2ae30d3ab771 changed source/narrative.html so the resource language element links to resource-definitions.html#Resource.language and the preceding language-of-resource link targets resource.html#language; current blame still traces the relevant narrative lines to that commit.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps narrative/xhtml type pages to source/narrative.html. The resource.html#language target exists in the active Resource page and explains Resource.language, BCP-47 language tags, narrative lang handling, and the current binding links. Later FHIR-39627 reconciliation aligned Resource.language with a required All Languages binding and Common Languages as only an additional starter binding, so applying the STU3 valueset-languages.html instruction literally would now point to the starter set rather than the full required language space. FHIR-18485 already audited the adjacent XHTML lang wording on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current narrative source has the originally broken link corrected, the remaining language-of-resource link lands on a valid current Resource language section, and a direct Common Languages-only link would be less accurate for current FHIR.

related_jiras.note: Adjacent narrative language guidance already has a no-change audit on the combined branch and confirms no broader narrative wording edit is needed here.
Later Resource.language binding work made All Languages required and Common Languages only a starter binding, affecting how the old direct valueset-languages target should be interpreted now.
